t.5.47.1: Then Hanumān of fearsome valor, amazed at his deed, his eyes copper-red with anger, gazed at the lord of the rākṣasas.
t.5.47.2: Him, resplendent and of great brilliance, shining with a precious, gleaming golden crown overlaid with a net of pearls.
t.5.47.3: With splendid golden ornaments, set with diamonds and shaped from priceless gems, as though fashioned by the mind alone.
t.5.47.4: He was clad in costly silk, smeared with red sandalwood paste, and finely anointed with many and varied decorative patterns.
t.5.47.5: With faces vast and striking, red-eyed and terrible to behold, with blazing, sharp, great fangs and pendulous lips.
t.5.47.6: He saw the hero of mighty energy, resplendent with his ten heads, like Mandara with its peaks swarming with many kinds of serpents.
t.5.47.7: He resembled a heap of blue collyrium, with a necklace shining upon his chest and a face like the full moon, like a rain-cloud accompanied by a flock of cranes.
t.5.47.9: He saw him seated upon a splendid throne, large, made of crystal, wondrous, adorned with an inlay of jewels, and spread with the finest coverings.
t.5.47.8: With his massive arms, on which armlets were fastened, smeared with the finest sandal paste and adorned with gleaming bracelets, looking like five-headed serpents.
t.5.47.10: He was attended on all sides, close at hand, by exceedingly adorned young women holding yak-tail fans in their hands.
t.5.47.11: He was attended by Durdhara, by Prahasta, by the rākṣasa Mahāpārśva, by ministers who knew the true essence of counsel, and by the minister Nikumbha.
t.5.47.13: He was attended by ministers versed in the essence of counsel and by other counsellors of auspicious understanding, just as the lord of the gods is attended by the gods.
t.5.47.12: Him, seated with four rākṣasas proud of their strength sitting close about him, like the world encircled by the four vast oceans entire.
t.5.47.14: Hanumān beheld the lord of the rākṣasas, exceedingly splendid, seated there like a water-laden rain cloud resting on the peak of Meru.
t.5.47.16: Then Hanumān, seeing the lord of the Rākṣasas shining resplendent, and bewildered by his splendour, reflected in his mind.
t.5.47.15: Though he was being harassed by those rākṣasas of terrible prowess, he was filled with the utmost wonder and gazed upon the lord of the rākṣasas.
t.5.47.17: Oh, what beauty! Oh, what fortitude! Oh, what strength! Oh, what splendor! Oh, how the king of the rākṣasas is endowed with every auspicious mark!
t.5.47.18: If unrighteousness were not so strong in him, this lord of the rākṣasas could be the protector even of the world of the gods, Śakra included.
t.5.47.19: Therefore the worlds, together with the immortals and the Dānavas, are indeed afraid of this one; for he, when enraged, is able to turn the whole world into a single ocean.
t.5.47.20: Having seen the majesty of the king of the Rākṣasas, whose might was boundless, the wise monkey thus pondered in many ways.
